title: Icon set before the style guide
caption: Text-only prompts: about, bluetooth, screenshot, display and trash drift to flat or straight-on views.

title: Icon set after the style guide
caption: Generated against the reference set (docs/ICONS.md): the outliers are now three-quarter view like the rest.

title: First Tracker desktop
caption: Volumes and Home beside the Deskbar, Trash in the corner. Labels were off-centre (centred galleys double-offset) and ~/Desktop items were missing.

title: Tracker and Get Info in dark mode
caption: Get Info rows on an exact LABEL_ROW + TIGHT grid, window sized to its content.

title: Tracker desktop, folder window and Get Info (light)
caption: Selected labels inverted as on BeOS, highlight balanced on cap height and baseline; links in italics; executable scripts get the executable icon.

title: Tracker list view
caption: Sortable ColumnListView with 16 px icons; count and free space in the bar beside the scroll bar.

title: Tracker: editing a name in place
caption: BeOS-style inline rename replaces the Rename dialog: the field sits on the label's own baseline and lines up with the selection highlight; the name without its extension starts selected.

title: Tracker: column view
caption: macOS-style column view (⌘4): one column per folder level, auto-hiding scroll bars, and a preview pane with an async thumbnail and file facts.

title: Tracker: Find
caption: Find takes focus on open, closes with ⌘W, shows home-relative locations and a baseline-aligned status.

title: Menus: shortcut glyphs on the baseline
caption: ⌘, ⇧ and arrows come from a fallback font; each is now laid out separately so it shares the item's baseline. The Trash is titled Trash.

title: Tracker: Find searches contents with ripgrep
caption: Find is built on ripgrep's crates (ignore + grep-searcher): parallel walk, smart case, .gitignore-aware, binary files skipped. Contents matches show the line number and text; live progress, Stop/Escape cancel.

title: Tracker Status: background file operations
caption: Copy, move, duplicate, Trash and Empty Trash run on worker threads (copy_file_range in chunks). Jobs longer than 0.4 s appear here with bytes, items, current file and time left; Stop cancels and removes the partial copy.

title: In-place reload: before
caption: Tracker (desktop + Home window, Home icon selected) and Deskbar under tabula-session, before rebuilding and running tabula-session reload.

title: In-place reload: after an upgrade
caption: After tabula-session reload with new tabula-session, app_server and Tracker binaries: the session re-executed itself, restarted app_server, and Tracker re-executed with its saved state. Pixel-identical to the screenshot before.

title: Tracker: live updates
caption: Folder windows, columns and the desktop now follow the disk as it changes via inotify, with no polling. Shot 120 ms after a shell wrote download.iso, renamed notes.md, deleted photo-02.jpg and made Archive. Selection and sort are kept; a deleted folder says so.

title: Terminal (light)
caption: Tabula Light scheme: 16 ANSI colours tuned for contrast on paper white, SGR attributes and truecolor, CJK/Greek/symbol fallback fonts, box drawing drawn as geometry (rounded and heavy), block elements, a kitty-protocol inline image, and a compiler-style path link.

title: Terminal (dark)
caption: The same session in Tabula Dark (graphite, soft pastels). The scheme follows the desktop theme, and OSC 10/11 colour queries answer from it, so TUIs like Claude Code choose the matching theme.

title: Quick Look: images
caption: Space on a selected item opens Quick Look; the window fits the screen (app_server now keeps newly sized windows on screen) and follows the selection.

title: Quick Look: source code (dark)
caption: Text and code coloured by syntax with the shared kit syntax palette (the same hues as Terminal), line numbers, virtualised rows.

title: Quick Look: every format (dark)
caption: Contact sheet: MP3/OGG with tags and playback, Markdown, JPEG, tar.gz, SVG, PDF (hayro), CSV, PNG, Word, zip, Rust. All decoded in process, with no helper tools.

title: Viewer: PDF form filling (light)
caption: Text, comb, combo, list box, radio and check fields filled in place, with a placed signature.

title: Viewer: PDF form in dark mode
caption: The same form in dark: Draw tool active, ink mark and Text tool date beside the signature.

title: Kit FilePanel: Export Flattened PDF
caption: BFilePanel-style Save panel: path popup, Home, Name/Size/Modified list, Save as field.

title: Quick Look pop-out to Viewer
caption: Popping a Quick Look out of Tracker opens the file in a standalone Viewer window (dark).

title: Twitcher (light)
caption: ⌘Tab held: app_server draws the BeOS Twitcher strip with each running app's icon and the chosen app's name.

title: Twitcher (dark)
caption: The same in dark mode.

title: Preferences panels (light)
caption: Appearance, Keyboard, Touchpad, Backgrounds, Display and About in light mode: one fixed-size window per panel with Defaults/Revert.

title: Preferences panels (dark)
caption: Appearance, Keyboard, Touchpad, Backgrounds, Display and About in dark mode: one fixed-size window per panel with Defaults/Revert.

title: Preferences launcher
caption: tabula-preferences with no argument: a grid of every panel.

title: Preferences ▸ Sound
caption: Output and input device, level and mute, read live from the sound server (light and dark).

title: Preferences ▸ Power
caption: Battery health and state, idle display-off and sleep times, caffeinated mode (light and dark).

title: Display ▸ Brightness
caption: The built-in display's brightness slider (simulated backlight in a headless session).

title: Deskbar caffeinated cup
caption: The tray cup: empty when sleep is allowed, full and steaming while caffeinated.

title: Lock screen
caption: tabula-lock over ext-session-lock: clock, date, and a BeOS panel asking for the password or Touch ID (dark).

title: Lock screen: wrong password
caption: A wrong password shakes the panel and says so (light); PAM runs on a thread.

title: Deskbar: Lock Screen
caption: Lock Screen in the Tabula menu; the off cup in the tray is now visible in dark mode.

title: Power: lock when the display turns off
caption: New option, on by default.

title: Screen saver modules
caption: BeOS R5's modules redrawn: BuyNow, Flip, Icons, Lens, Lissart, Message, Spiral, Spots, StringTheme, SuperString (plus Blackness).

title: Preferences: Screen Saver, Fade
caption: R5's Fade tab: run after, turn off screen, password lock, Fade now / Don't fade corners.

title: Preferences: Screen Saver, Modules
caption: Live preview in the monitor, module list, settings and Test (dark).

title: Screen saver over the lock screen
caption: Locks underneath after the delay; the first input ends the saver and shows the lock.

title: Screenshot (light)
caption: Haiku-style Screenshot app: preview, capture options, name/format/folder; restored after an in-place reload.

title: Screenshot: active window (dark)
caption: Active-window capture with the tab's shape kept; JPEG into a folder chosen with the new folder panel.

title: DeskCalc (light)
caption: R5's keypad under an expression line; 2*(3+4) worked out.

title: DeskCalc scientific (dark)
caption: Haiku's scientific rows above R5's keys; options in the context menu.

title: StyledEdit: fonts, sizes and colours
caption: StyledEdit with a bold red word and a 24 pt Comfortaa word in the system font's line; styles live in the file's user.tabula.styles attribute, the text stays plain.

title: StyledEdit: selection keeps its colours
caption: egui paints selected text in one colour; StyledEdit draws the selected glyphs again over the highlight in their own colours.

title: StyledEdit in dark mode after a reload
caption: Unsaved text and styles came back after app_server reloaded and the app re-executed; default text follows the theme, explicit colours stay.

title: Alerts get their icons
caption: The warning, stop, info and idea alert icons were missing from the set (every alert drew none); generated against the reference set.

title: Activity Monitor: graphs
caption: CPU, memory and cache with Total System Power from hwmon; network and disk rates below.

title: Activity Monitor: processes
caption: Sortable process list with search by name or ID and an owner filter.

title: Activity Monitor: permission alert
caption: Force Quit of another user's process shows a stop alert; nothing is signalled.

title: Activity Monitor: dark mode
caption: Graphs and legend in dark mode.

title: Alerts open over their window
caption: Alerts are children of the focused window; app_server centres them across it a quarter of the way down, as BAlert did.

title: Date & Time: Deskbar clock
caption: 24-hour clock, seconds and weekday options; Deskbar follows the setting live.

title: Date & Time: time zones
caption: Every timedated zone with its offset and local time, searchable; opens on the current zone.

title: Date & Time (dark)
caption: Calendar and clock face; disabled while network time is on.

title: polkit agent
caption: Authentication Required: polkit message, Touch ID through PAM first (fprintd), new padlock icon.

title: polkit agent: password
caption: After the fingerprint times out PAM asks for the password; the field takes focus.

title: Preferences: Network
caption: Wi-Fi networks in range with security and signal; the one in use ticked, with Disconnect and Forget.

title: Preferences: Bluetooth
caption: Power, search (30 s), named and paired devices with type, status and battery; pairing questions appear in the panel.

title: Preferences: Touch ID
caption: Enrolled fingers, add one (likeliest finger first), remove with confirmation (fake sensor).

title: Touch ID: enrolling (dark)
caption: Progress per touch with the sensor guidance; Cancel stops the sensor.

title: Wallpaper drawn by app_server
caption: Backgrounds sets a JPEG XL wallpaper; app_server decodes and scales it to cover the output on a worker thread and draws it under every surface.

title: Choose a Wallpaper panel
caption: The kit FilePanel as a child of Backgrounds, limited to picture types, kept on screen when wider than its parent.

title: Backgrounds in dark mode
caption: The chosen wallpaper survives an in-place reload via About Tabula, Restart Tabula.

title: Display: resolution with revert countdown
caption: HEADLESS-1 switched to 1920 by 1200; its right-hand neighbour moved with the edge; Keep or Revert, else it reverts after 15 s.

title: Display: arranged screens, dark
caption: Two headless screens stacked by dragging in the map; the lower one follows when the upper changes size.

title: Display: Identify
caption: Each screen shows its name, connector and mode in a raised panel for 4 s.

title: Rotated main display
caption: HEADLESS-2 rotated 90 degrees and made the main display; Deskbar and the desktop icons moved to it and re-laid out in portrait.

title: Haiku system cursors
caption: All 28 of Haiku app_server cursors drawn by the new tabula-hvif renderer at 1x, 1.5x and 2x on light and dark grounds, with the soft offset shadow. ResizeWest is mirrored from ResizeEast since the upstream data duplicates it.

title: Cursors in a session
caption: Headless 2x session: StyledEdit asks for the text cursor over cursor-shape-v1, the desktop shows the hand, the window frame shows the resize arrow.

title: Level indicator
caption: app_server panel for the brightness and volume keys and Ctrl+Cmd+A caffeinated, light and dark, 2x.

title: Deskbar Stay Awake menu
caption: Right-click the cup (also in the Tabula menu): until turned off, 1 to 8 hours, even with the lid closed, Allow Sleep with the end time. The menu now flips to stay on screen.

title: Keyboard backlight
caption: Keyboard illumination keys raise the backlight with the level indicator; Preferences Keyboard has a Backlight slider that follows it. Turns off with the display.

title: Display mirroring
caption: A display set to mirror another leaves the arrangement; only resolution, refresh and Use as remain

title: Back to extended
caption: Choosing Extended desktop puts the display back beside the other with its full settings

title: Terminal Find window
caption: Find in the scrollback: case, whole words, wrap-around, backwards

title: Terminal found it
caption: The match is selected and scrolled into view; Find Again steps on

title: Colour emoji in Terminal
caption: COLRv1 emoji painted natively: sequences, skin tones, flags, keycaps, on any background

title: Icons for document kinds
caption: Spreadsheet, presentation, word processing, PDF and font files get their own icons

title: Viewer zoom and pan
caption: Images load at full resolution in Viewer: Actual Size, pinch and command-scroll zoom about the pointer, drag to pan

title: Viewer: AVIF
caption: AVIF decoded natively with avif-parse and the BSD-licensed rav1d AV1 decoder, with our own YUV to RGB; HEIC through heifer and Ogg Opus playback through opus-decoder land in the same change

title: Viewer: video playback
caption: H.264 in mp4 and Matroska decoded with OpenH264 a few frames ahead and shown against a clock that follows the sound; play, pause, seek and replay, and the screen stays awake while it plays

title: Viewer: AV1 video
caption: AV1 in WebM and Matroska plays through rav1d with Opus sound; the poster frame decodes too, and the YUV to RGB conversion moved to fixed point tables (1080p at 72 frames a second)

title: Network: joining enterprise Wi-Fi
caption: A sheet for 802.1X networks: PEAP or TTLS with username and password, or TLS with certificate and key, the CA and a domain; shown with made-up networks. Tab now moves between text fields in every kit form

title: NetPositive in dark mode
caption: The new Servo based browser: tabs, toolbar and location field follow the theme while pages stay light

title: NetPositive error page
caption: Network errors answer in haiku, as NetPositive did, picked at random from six new verses

title: Passwords: Password Generator
caption: Random, memorable and PIN recipes with a live strength meter; Use fills the field it was opened from.

title: Passwords: a 1Password browser
caption: Tabula's password manager, on its own Rust 1Password SDK over the desktop app's integration socket (shown against the test fake): vaults and categories, items, and the selected item's fields.

title: Passwords: locked
caption: Opens locked and locks after idle; Touch ID (fprintd) or the account password (PAM) unlocks it.

title: NetPositive: logins from Passwords
caption: The key button lists the page's logins from Passwords (starting and unlocking it if need be) and fills the chosen one in.

title: NetPositive: offer to update a login
caption: After a sign-in with a changed password, NetPositive offers to update the login in Passwords; a new one gets Save.

title: NetPositive: save a passkey
caption: A page's navigator.credentials.create() asks in a bar; Passwords makes and keeps the key.

title: NetPositive: sign in with a passkey
caption: navigator.credentials.get() finds the site's passkeys in Passwords and asks before Passwords signs.

title: NetPositive: choosing a passkey
caption: With several passkeys for the site, the bar has a pop-up to choose the account.

title: Passwords: a passkey in a login
caption: Passkeys live in a Passkey section of a 1Password login: credential ID, relying party, user, and the concealed P-256 key.

title: NetPositive: Find
caption: Edit ▸ Find… (⌘F) and Find Again (⌘G): a BeOS Find window; the match is selected and scrolled to the middle.

title: NetPositive: Downloads
caption: Downloads go straight to ~/Downloads on a worker thread: links the page can't show, download links (also blob: and data: ones made by script), and Download Linked File / Download Image in the context menu. The Downloads window shows live progress and rate, with Stop, Retry, Open and Show.

title: NetPositive: scroll bars
caption: Servo draws no scroll bars, so a script reports where the page is scrolled and NetPositive draws BeOS ones beside it (a new kit ScrollBar): the vertical bar always, the horizontal one when the page is wider than the window. Dragging, paging and the arrows scroll the page.

title: NetPositive: tab icons
caption: Tabs show the page's favicon (scaled on the CPU to a crisp 16-point icon), or a plain document for pages without one.

title: Preferences: Backgrounds' BColorControl
caption: The desktop colour is now set with the kit's new ColorControl, BeOS's BColorControl: grey, red, green and blue ramps from black with draggable markers, and number fields.

title: NetPositive: colour picker
caption: <input type=color> opens a Choose a Colour sheet with the kit ColorControl; OK sets the page's colour and fires its input and change events (Servo 0.7 fires none).

title: NetPositive: dark pages
caption: In dark and night modes pages that support dark (color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme) go dark, canvas included; pages that don't stay black on white with light form controls and links.

title: NetPositive: light page, dark desktop
caption: A page with no colour scheme in dark mode: Servo would have drawn it with light text and dark controls on white; it now keeps the light scheme.

title: NetPositive: audio and video
caption: Video and audio elements in pages play with Tabula's own decoders (H.264/AV1 in MP4 and WebM, Opus, AAC, MP3 and more) through a native servo-media backend; sound goes to the sound server in process.

title: NetPositive: a page over its memory
caption: A page that runs away with memory meets its unit's MemoryMax (512 MiB here, for the test) and is OOM-killed alone; the bar says why, over the crash page.

title: NetPositive: a stuck page
caption: Pages run in content processes, each a systemd unit with its own memory limit and CPU weight. A tab whose page stops answering for ten seconds gets this bar; Stop Page kills just that process and the tab shows the crash page.

title: NetPositive: a page of 120 big photos
caption: 120 pictures of 2400×1600, 1.8 GB once decoded. The page's process now holds only their files (60 MB, was every bitmap), and the painter decodes a picture only while it's drawn, within 128 MB shared by every page, so the whole browser stays near 600 MB however long the page.

title: NetPositive: a call, end to end
caption: Two RTCPeerConnections in one page, talking through NetPositive's own WebRTC (webrtc-rs, in process). The fake camera's test card goes out as H.264 (openh264) and comes back decoded on the right; the microphone goes as Opus and plays; a data channel carries text and bytes both ways; getStats() counts the pictures.

title: Deskbar: a new build is ready
caption: tabula-session watches the tree Tabula was built in. Once a build finishes with newer programs, a green arrow appears in Deskbar's tray; clicking it asks before installing them and reloading the session in place (windows stay open).

title: NetPositive: the WebRTC samples' peer connection
caption: The official webrtc.github.io 'Peer connection' sample, unmodified: the test camera (left) goes through two RTCPeerConnections and comes back decoded (right), connected in 281 ms.

title: Passwords: choose your 1Password account
caption: Setting up Passwords now lists the accounts signed in to the 1Password app (read from its local account summaries), with email and sign-in address, instead of asking for a name or UUID. Another account still takes one by hand.

title: Keyring prompts are Tabula's
caption: gnome-keyring asks for the login keyring's password through a system prompter; the authentication agent now is that prompter (gcr's protocol and encrypted secret exchange, in Rust), so unlocking it for gh or a browser is a Tabula alert, not GTK's gcr-prompter. A wrong password comes back with the keyring's warning.

title: Shells that outlive Terminal
caption: Terminal's shells now run in tabula-termd, one per display, which keeps each screen too. Quit Terminal, or have it crash or upgrade, and the next one reopens a window on every shell as it was, scrollback, vim and all. Terminal ▸ Terminal Daemon… shows it and its shells, and can restart it in place (shells kept) or start it over.

title: Images survive Terminal crashes
caption: Terminal was killed after showing a kitty image; tabula-termd relaunched it and replayed the screen, image included. ⌘R also reaches the shell now (reverse history search).

title: Zoom leaves Deskbar alone
caption: A zoomed window now stops 4 px short of Deskbar, as on BeOS, instead of running under it.

title: Right-click in text fields
caption: Every text field now has Cut, Copy, Paste and Select All on right-click (keeping the selection), and double/triple-click select a word or the whole line, here in NetPositive's location field.

title: Brightness for every display
caption: Preferences ▸ Display now has a brightness slider for each display whose brightness can be set, external monitors too (the Studio Display over USB). Every display starts at full brightness unless you've set a level for it.

title: Tile windows from the keyboard
caption: ⇧⌘← and ⇧⌘→ tile the window into half the display, ⇧⌘↑/↓ the top or bottom; ⌃⌘↵ tiles every window on the display (here, three); quarters, thirds, centering and moving to the next display too. Space between them and at the edges is set in Preferences.

title: Keyboard shortcuts in Preferences
caption: Keyboard ▸ Shortcuts lists the desktop's shortcuts, with the space around tiled windows. Click one and type new keys (here Left half became ⌃⌥L); keys taken from another shortcut are said, and Default Keys puts them all back.

title: Notifications
caption: A native notification centre: apps' notifications (org.freedesktop.Notifications) appear as cards in the lower right with the app's icon, the summary, the body and their actions. A click is the default action; they go by themselves unless critical, and wait while the pointer is over them.

title: NetPositive: web notifications
caption: Sites can show notifications: the first time one asks, a bar over its tab offers Allow or Don’t Allow (remembered per site); allowed notifications appear in the desktop's notification centre, and a click brings the tab forward.

title: NetPositive: dark pages
caption: View ▸ Dark Pages (Automatic, the default, follows the desktop; Always; Never). Each frame is redrawn on the GPU through a shader that turns lightness around and keeps hues, so every page goes dark, blank ones included; pictures, video and canvases are pre-inverted with the CSS filter the shader undoes, and pages that are dark already are left alone. Left: Never; right: Always.

title: Command palette (⌘Space)
caption: ⌘Space opens a Raycast-style palette over everything: apps, the front app's menu commands, files, Passwords items, Preferences, windows, a calculator and every desktop shortcut with its keys, so typing "half" doubles as a reminder of ⇧⌘←.

title: NetPositive: dark pages, the Chrome way
caption: Dark pages redone as Chrome's Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents: WebRender recolours what each thing is (light backgrounds and borders go dark, dark text light, by CIELAB lightness with hue kept), so photos, gradients and coloured buttons keep their true colours and only icons that Chrome's classifier would flip are inverted. Left: light desktop; right: dark.

title: Quick Look: F for fullscreen
caption: In Quick Look, F fills the screen with the preview and F again puts it back in its window at the size it had (Cx::set_fullscreen, new in the kit).

title: Tracker: column view scrolls sideways
caption: Columns wider than the window scroll sideways with the touchpad, Shift+wheel or a scroll bar along the bottom, and stay where they were put; the view only follows the keyboard when the selection moves to another column.

title: NetPositive learns login fields
caption: The field menu now lists the page's logins at once (fetched when the page loads). Filling an odd field from it — here 'who are you' as the username — is remembered for that page, so the key button fills the same field next time. Hidden decoy fields, as on Google's sign-in, are skipped.

title: Preferences ▸ Tracker
caption: New Tracker windows open in column view by default; Preferences has a Tracker panel to choose the view new windows open in, and Tracker follows a change at once.

title: Deskbar: a click lists an app's windows
caption: Clicking an application with more than one window in Deskbar now opens its window menu to pick one (or Show All); with one window it comes forward at once, as before.

title: Find: Space for Quick Look
caption: In Tracker's Find window, Space shows the selected result in Quick Look and the arrow keys step through the results, as in a folder window. A space typed into the Find field still goes into the query.

title: Tracker: Open in Terminal
caption: File ▸ Open in Terminal, and the context menus, open a new Terminal window in the folder shown, or in the right-clicked folder (here alpha).

title: Passwords: setup offers sync or local
caption: Passwords now keeps its own encrypted store. The first time, it asks whether to sync with a 1Password account (both ways) or keep items only on this computer.

title: Passwords: its own store, synced with 1Password
caption: Items are read from the local encrypted store at once; 1Password is only for syncing, in the background. The status line shows the last sync.

title: Passwords: changes wait while 1Password is away
caption: With 1Password not running, changes are kept and the status line counts what's still to send; they go up on the next sync.

title: Videos with B-frames play properly
caption: H.264 High videos with B-frames (most from screen recorders and x264) played with good sound but a picture that jumped and stalled: OpenH264 was asked to flush a picture after every packet, which broke reordering, so every B-frame failed. Now every picture decodes, in display order and in step with the sound (edit lists applied); seeking WebM/AV1 lands on the right frame too.

title: NetPositive asks before quitting
caption: Quitting NetPositive (or closing a window) with several tabs open, or downloads still running, now asks first, so a stray ⌘Q doesn't throw the tabs away.

title: Passwords asks before syncing anything
caption: Syncing with 1Password now works out every change first, both ways (adding, changing, archiving, deleting, with the parts that differ), and makes none until you approve them in Review Sync. Automatic syncs only say how many changes are waiting.

title: Restore from the Trash
caption: Items in the Trash can go back where they came from: Restore in the File menu or an item's menu puts them back in their folders (made again if gone), and never over something new in their place.

title: Passwords: every vault, and sync problems you can read
caption: 1Password won't let other apps read archived items, and one archived item failed a whole batch of fifty, so most of Personal and Private never arrived. Now only active items are fetched, an item archived there is archived here from its listing, and a failed batch is retried one item at a time. What still can't sync is listed in a Sync Problems window, grouped by vault, each with its reason, instead of a wall of red text.

title: Passwords: several 1Password accounts
caption: Passwords now syncs with every 1Password account you tick (File ▸ 1Password Accounts…), in one review. The sidebar lists each account's vaults under its name, a vault is named with its account wherever it could be confused, and removing an account asks first and only removes its items from this computer.

title: Drag and drop
caption: Files drag between Tracker's views, the desktop, other apps and other Wayland programs, BeOS-style: a see-through picture with the name, folders light up to take them, move within a disk and copy across, a right-button drag asks Move/Copy/Link. Desktop icons stay where you put them. Drop a file on Terminal to type its path (an image into Claude Code).

title: Band selection in lists
caption: Dragging from a row's other columns, or from below the rows, draws a selection band in Tracker's list view and in every kit list (⇧ or ⌘ adds; it scrolls on near the edges). The column view does the same from below a column's items.

title: Security preferences
caption: Preferences ▸ Security holds how Passwords keeps its secrets: sync with 1Password automatically or only when asked, lock after idle, lock when the screen locks, and how soon copied secrets leave the clipboard. Passwords follows them live.

title: Google Chrome, installed on first use
caption: Google Chrome is one of Tabula's applications. The first time it is opened, Tabula offers to download it from Google's own repository, checks it against the repository's checksum, unpacks it natively into the home folder and starts it, drawing with Wayland in a Tabula window.

title: GTK and Chrome in Tabula's colours
caption: The desktop portals now start in a real session. GTK 3, GTK 4 and libadwaita apps take Tabula's palette, fonts and close-left/zoom-right buttons, in light and dark, and Chrome opens with Tabula's tab and frame instead of its own buttons.

title: Log Viewer
caption: A native reader for your journal: Tabula's own programs (or everything), by level and time, with Find, live tail, Show in Context and syntax highlighting on every line. Also a --print command line for agents.

title: Hide window, anywhere
caption: ⌘M hides the window in front, Tabula's or any other app's, and Hide window is a ⌘Space command (it finds "minimize" too). Change the keys in Preferences ▸ Keyboard.

title: Long menus scroll
caption: A menu taller than the screen fits it now, with BeOS scroll arrows at its ends: rest the pointer on one to scroll, or use the wheel or the arrow keys.

title: Notifications, grouped
caption: Notifications now gather under their app as on Haiku, keep bold, italics and links, show progress, take a reply in place, and wear a blue edge when important or a red one for errors. A click hands the app an activation token so its window comes forward.

title: Notification history
caption: The History window (Deskbar's bell, or tabula-notifications --history): every notification newest first, kept across a restart. Click to act on it (or bring the app forward), × to forget one; Do Not Disturb and Clear All along the top.

title: Deskbar's notification bell
caption: The bell counts unread notifications; click for the history, right-click for Do Not Disturb (now, for an hour, until morning) and the settings. Struck through while quiet.

title: Preferences ▸ Notifications
caption: Do Not Disturb by hand or every day at set times, how long banners stay, and per-app banners, sounds and history (apps appear once they have notified). Dark theme.

title: GApplication notifications
caption: tabula-notifications now also serves GLib's org.gtk.Notifications: a GApplication's notification (here a test app's, with an app.reply button) shows like any other, and its actions run on the app over org.freedesktop.Application.

title: Tracker says when a long copy is done
caption: Through the kit's new notify API: a copy or move that ran 10 s or more posts “Finished copying …”; clicking it shows the folder.

title: Viewer: crop a picture
caption: Image ▸ Crop… puts a frame over the picture: drag one out, move it or pull its edges; the size shows below and the rest dims. Crop (or Return) keeps it, and the title says the picture is edited until it's saved.

title: Viewer: Adjust Size
caption: Image ▸ Adjust Size… resizes the picture, keeping its proportions unless asked not to. Rotate, flip, crop and resize can all be undone, and File ▸ Save writes the picture back in its own format (Save As for another).

title: Quick Look rotates pictures
caption: Quick Look's footer has Rotate Left and Right (⌘L and ⌘R), which turn the picture and save it at once, as on the Mac. Anything more opens in Viewer.

title: Preferences: Backup
caption: Export saves every Tabula setting and piece of saved state in one .tabula-backup file. Import shows what a backup holds, app by app, and asks before replacing anything; the settings as they were are saved first.

title: Backup, dark
caption: The Backup panel in the dark theme.

title: Backups have their own icon
caption: Tracker shows .tabula-backup files with the new backup icon; opening one shows it in Preferences ▸ Backup, ready to import.

title: Drag a picture out of Viewer
caption: A picture that fits Viewer's window drags out as its file (and, for PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP, the picture itself for programs that take one). Quick Look does the same, from the picture or its footer's icon. Dropping it back into its own folder is refused.

title: Drop files on an app in Deskbar
caption: Files dragged onto a running application in Deskbar highlight it and open with it when dropped.

title: Spring-loaded folders
caption: Rest a drag on a folder for a second and it opens, so the drag can go on into it (here a file dragged onto Dest, whose window opened under the pointer).

title: Views scroll under a drag
caption: A drag held near the top or bottom of any scrolling view scrolls it on, faster nearer the edge, so a drop can reach what was out of view.

title: GTK windows wear Tabula's chrome
caption: Plain GTK 3 and GTK 4 windows (no headerbar) now get Tabula's tab and frame: app_server speaks KDE's server-decoration protocol, which is how GTK asks for server-side decorations.

title: Drag an application out of Deskbar
caption: Dragging an application's row out of Deskbar leaves a link to it where it's dropped, named and drawn as the application; opening the link starts it.

title: Drag text in and out of text fields
caption: Press on selected text and drag it: within a StyledEdit document it moves (styles and all), into another field or app it's copied, onto a folder it becomes a clipping. A caret shows where it will land.
